Variance of the provider effects for a Wald test

Source: R/model_linear_fe.R, R/model_logistic_fe.R
gamma_variance.Rd

Two model-based variances of a fixed provider effect \(\hat\gamma_i\) are available. The "case_mix" variance is that of \(\hat\gamma_i + \bar x_i^\top\hat\beta\), the provider's outcome (log-odds or mean) at its own average case mix \(\bar x_i\); it does not depend on where the covariates are centred and is the default of test(). The "full" variance is the \((\gamma_i,\gamma_i)\) element of the inverse information, \(1/I_{ii} + \bar z_i^\top \mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta)\bar z_i\); it is the variance of the outcome at \(Z = 0\) and changes with the origin of the covariates, so it is only appropriate when the null value is an external constant stated in the same coding.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'linear_fe'
gamma_variance(fit, type = c("case_mix", "full"), ...)

gamma_variance(fit, type = c("case_mix", "full"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'logistic_fe'
gamma_variance(fit, type = c("case_mix", "full"), ...)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted by fit_logistic_fe() or fit_linear_fe().

type

"case_mix" (default) or "full".

...

unused.

Value

A named numeric vector, one variance per provider.

Details

For the logistic model \(\bar z_i\) is the \(N p (1 - p)\)-weighted mean covariate and the case-mix variance is \(1/I_{ii} + (\bar z_i - \bar x_i)^\top \mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta) (\bar z_i - \bar x_i)\); for the linear model \(\bar z_i = \bar x_i\) and the case-mix variance is exactly \(\hat\sigma^2 / n_i\).
